newsitem.title: UK: Severn Trent saw household savings in bid.
newsitem.headline: Severn Trent saw household savings in bid.

text.p: British water company Severn Trent said its blocked bid for South West Water would have meant cuts of 27 stg per year for households in the South West.
In a statement, the company said it believed that its proposed merger "would have brought efficiencies benefiting shareholders and customers without any damage to the regulatory system."
The UK's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said earlier on Friday it would block Severn Trent's proposed bid and one from rival Wessex Water because they were against the public interest.
"I find the report's focus on the regulatory issues at the expense of real benefits to customers and shareholders quite extraordinary," Severn Trent chief executive Vic Cocker said in the statement.
"We will continue to concentrate on improving our operational performance and sharing the benefits with shareholders and customers," he added.
South West Water responded to the DTI's decision by announcing it would give customers a 15 stg rebate in June 1997 and said it would raise its interim dividend 20.4 percent to 11.8 pence per share.
